content.jointProblem: Can a site-specific, label-free baseline model of Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP traffic be built from long-term normal captures, coupled with drift detection and a low false-alarm threshold policy, so that ProtoSense flags behaviour that departs from normal in a way that can be explained to a plant manager? The first experiment would test whether the researcher's semi-supervised one-class and drift-adaptation methods transfer from sensor time-series to protocol-level network traffic.

rationale.text: Rakić has a published semi-supervised one-class framework designed for exactly the situation ArmaturaSec describes: mostly unlabelled streams with only a small fraction of labelled anomalies.

sources.quote: proposes a constrained OC-SVM variant that incorporates labelled anomalies as must-outside constraints during kernel optimisation

rationale.text: She works directly on concept drift adaptation in streaming fault data, which is what a site-specific normal baseline needs when plant operations change.

sources.quote: ADWIN combined with ensemble voting detects sudden drift with a median latency of 47 samples
methods for handling concept drift and label scarcity

rationale.text: She has demonstrated learning under extreme label scarcity with uncertainty-filtered self-training, reaching near-supervised performance from very few labels.

sources.quote: Starting from 2% labelled data, the filtered self-training approach reaches 91% of fully supervised F1 performance

rationale.text: Her threshold-selection work targets the exact failure ArmaturaSec suffered in deployment — tuning the operating point against an acceptable false-positive rate on heavily imbalanced data.

sources.quote: Recommendations are given as a decision guide indexed by imbalance ratio and acceptable false-positive rate.
the chapter argues for systematic reporting of AUPRC and G-mean alongside domain-relevant cost measures

rationale.text: She has hands-on experience deploying detection pipelines on constrained edge hardware, matching ProtoSense's on-appliance inference requirement.

sources.quote: The quantised convolutional network fits within 200 KB and achieves 97% of its full-precision AUPRC while meeting a 5 ms per-window latency budget
Olivera Rakić leads the work package on model compression and edge deployment

rationale.text: Her running DRIFTGUARD project already couples semi-supervised classification with drift detection and targeted labelling, which maps onto the ProtoSense baseline-plus-drift requirement.

sources.quote: a semi-supervised classifier is coupled with a lightweight drift detector

rationale.text: She has prior industrial engagement auditing the validation practice of an operating classifier, relevant to rebuilding trust after the false-positive episode.

sources.quote: audit the evaluation practices of their existing predictive maintenance classifier, resulting in a revised validation protocol

constraints.text: The method must operate without any labelled attack examples, since the company has none and supervised classifiers already failed.

sources.quote: we have zero examples of malicious traffic and supervised classifiers are useless to us
raises a flag when behaviour drifts from that baseline

constraints.text: Work depends on access to the multi-terabyte normal-traffic archives and the hardware bench, released under NDA.

sources.quote: we have collected several terabytes of captures from consenting clients over the past three years
access to our traffic archives, our hardware bench, and our existing firmware codebase under NDA

constraints.text: Inference must run on the appliance itself without harming forwarding performance, so model size and per-window latency are hard limits.

sources.quote: on-device anomaly detection without affecting packet forwarding latency

constraints.text: Alerts must be explainable in plain language to a plant manager, not only statistically scored.

sources.quote: we can explain to a plant manager in plain language

constraints.text: The false-positive rate must be kept low enough that clients do not disable alerting again.

sources.quote: it flagged so many false positives in real deployments that clients started switching the alerts off

constraints.text: The researcher's availability for a new long-term commitment is limited and explicitly unknown before mid-2025.

sources.quote: has limited capacity for new long-term commitments before mid-2025

risks: Transfer gap: all cited detection results come from vibration, SCADA, chemical reactor, semiconductor, server-counter and smart-meter data, not from Modbus TCP or BACnet/IP packet streams; the one-class work touched network intrusion logs, but only as aggregate flow features. Whether these methods hold on protocol-level traffic is untested and must be the first experiment.

Evaluation is fundamentally weak without any confirmed attacks: detection quality cannot be measured against ground truth unless controlled fault or attack traffic is injected on the hardware-in-the-loop bench with PLC simulators.

Drift in OT networks comes from firmware updates, maintenance and operational changes rather than sensor wear; the drift detectors cited were validated on industrial process streams and may not transfer.
Explainability to a plant manager is a stated need but no cited work demonstrates plain-language explanation of network anomaly decisions.
False-positive behaviour in real customer deployments is unproven; the earlier supervised attempt failed there and clients already distrust alerts.

The researcher has no documented Modbus/BACnet or OT network security background, and the company has only one engineer with six months of self-study in anomaly detection, so protocol-domain assumptions may go unchecked.
The researcher's overall availability is unknown and she already co-supervises two PhD students, so scope and timeline may not be sustainable.
The 2021 student project with a Novi Sad faculty was not continued formally, suggesting a prior mismatch in sustaining academic-industry collaborations.
questions: The researcher lists both industrial PhD supervision and joint projects as open: which format does she prefer for this task, and does the company's single anomaly-detection engineer serve as the internal technical contact she asks for?
What is her actual availability and earliest start date given the two co-supervised DRIFTGUARD students and the stated limit before mid-2025?
Can ArmaturaSec generate labelled test events by injecting controlled attacks or faults on the hardware-in-the-loop bench with physical PLC simulators, and under what conditions?
What are the concrete memory and per-window latency budgets on the planned security-processor hardware variant, and what false-positive rate per site-day would clients accept?
What do the NDA terms allow regarding the traffic archives, the firmware codebase and publication of results or a benchmark dataset?
What form must the plain-language explanation take for a plant manager, and who on the company side validates that it is actionable?
How will normal baseline data be segmented across client sites, and is per-site model training and update on the appliance acceptable?
